title: Belafonte and the Ella-Ellington special: Jones writes the strings
summary: Jones wrote strings for Duke Ellington's augmented orchestra in a Burbank television show; Duke himself did not write for strings.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: The two Harry Belafonte television shows you did were, 'New York 19,' and, 'The Strolling '20s.' We talked about, 'The Strolling '20s,' but I don't think we talked about the name of the other show. The Ella Fitzgerald special.
That was -- Oh, that was with Ellington.
Oh, yeah.
If I can remember. We were still a package then.
Uh-huh.
And Duke Ellington with strings, which sounded very good. And we had some -- Ellington augmented his orchestra and -- to have some of the studio men in there, you know?
And you did the string writing?
Yeah.
Duke usually had someone else write for strings, didn't he? He didn't do any string writing, did he?
No, he didn't do it.
He had you, he had Calvin Jackson a long time ago, and he had different people. Did Strayhorn write for strings ever?
Oh, I think Strayhorn -- when did he pass?
1967, I believe. As I recall.
Oh, yeah. Well -- but I think Strayhorn was still back east at that time.
He was sick in '65.
Yeah. And I think this was about around '65. We did it out here. Did it out in Burbank, you know?

Uh-huh. I was trying to remember who else Duke had used to arrange for strings before you were doing it, and I really can't remember, except a long time ago Calvin, but I know that Duke usually called in someone else, someone compatible --
With what he was doing.
Uh-huh.
Yes.
